name: luaradio
desc: Lightweight, embeddable flow graph signal processing framework for SDR
why: A flow-graph signal processing framework for SDR written in Lua, a lovely way to build radio pipelines and inspect the signals.

brief.what_it_is: LuaRadio is a lightweight, embeddable flow graph signal processing framework for software-defined radio. It ships a set of source, sink, and processing blocks, plus a Lua API for defining and running flow graphs, creating blocks, and creating data types. Flow graphs are written as Lua scripts that connect blocks such as an RTL-SDR source, a tuner, an FM discriminator, filters, and an audio sink, then call run(). It can also be run through built-in command-line receivers such as rx_wbfm and rx_ax25. It is built on LuaJIT, and its binary is under 750 KB including LuaJIT.
brief.why_it_exists: The README positions it for rapidly prototyping software radios, modulation and demodulation utilities, and signal processing experiments. It also says it can be embedded into existing radio applications as a user-scriptable signal processing engine.
brief.how_it_works: Blocks are written in pure Lua and connected into a flow graph with CompositeBlock():connect(...), then executed with :run(). Blocks can use LuaJIT's FFI to wrap optional external libraries such as VOLK and liquid-dsp for acceleration and for talking to SDR hardware. The README does not describe the scheduler in detail.

brief.install_notes: LuaJIT is required, and LuaRadio can run directly from a git clone with ./luaradio. Optional but recommended for real-time work: liquid-dsp, VOLK, and fftw, which you confirm with --platform showing them as true. Packages exist for Arch Linux (AUR package luaradio), macOS via Homebrew or MacPorts (package luaradio), and other methods are in docs/1.installation.md. Running the wideband FM example needs an RTL-SDR dongle, and its audio sink uses PulseAudio. Unit tests need busted installed through LuaRocks for Lua 5.1.
brief.standout: It is a small, dependency-light SDR flow graph engine where the whole signal chain is ordinary Lua, with the FFI used to reach native DSP libraries. The README says it runs on a Raspberry Pi 3, and it offers an embeddable C library so other applications can script their signal processing.
brief.status: Unknown as of this read, leaning quiet. The README shows a passing tests badge and an MIT license badge but gives no release date or recent-commit information, and the homepage copyright reads 2016-2021. I did not check the release page or commit history.
brief.caveats: Primarily supports Linux. FreeBSD and macOS are described as experimental for real-time and audio sink support. Real-time performance depends on the optional liquid-dsp, VOLK, and fftw libraries. The wideband FM example also needs specific hardware (an RTL-SDR) and PulseAudio. The README does not list a feature roadmap beyond a wiki link.
quotes: LuaRadio is a lightweight, embeddable flow graph signal processing framework for software-defined radio.

LuaRadio blocks are written in pure Lua, but can use LuaJIT's FFI to wrap external libraries, like VOLK, liquid-dsp, and others, for computational acceleration, sophisticated processing, and interfacing with SDR hardware.
LuaRadio and all of its examples run great on the Raspberry Pi 3 with Arch Linux or Raspbian.

entry.title: LuaRadio
entry.tldr: A tiny software-defined radio framework where you wire up receivers as plain Lua scripts: source, filters, demodulator, audio out, then run().
entry.deeper_look:
LuaRadio is a flow graph signal processing framework for software-defined radio. A flow graph is a chain of blocks, each doing one job: read samples from an RTL-SDR, tune to a frequency, filter, demodulate FM, play audio. In LuaRadio you write that chain as an ordinary Lua script, connect the blocks with `CompositeBlock():connect(...)`, and call `:run()`.

The README pitches it for rapid prototyping of software radios, modulation and demodulation utilities, and signal processing experiments. It can also be embedded in existing radio applications as a user-scriptable processing engine. The whole thing, LuaJIT included, is under 750 KB.

Blocks are written in pure Lua, but LuaJIT's FFI lets them wrap native libraries such as VOLK and liquid-dsp for speed and for talking to SDR hardware. That is the idea worth stealing: a radio receiver is just a small readable graph of stages, and you can reshape it by editing a few lines. It also ships built-in command-line receivers such as `rx_wbfm` and `rx_ax25` if you would rather listen than build.

The README says it runs well on a Raspberry Pi 3, which makes it a plausible base for a small dedicated radio box.
entry.install:
brew install luaradio
# Running the FM example needs an RTL-SDR dongle and PulseAudio for the audio sink. The brew formula pulls in luajit, fftw and liquid-dsp.

entry.caveats: Primarily a Linux tool, with macOS described as experimental for real-time and audio output; project activity looked quiet, with the homepage copyright reading 2016-2021.
